Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Surakarta. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Surakarta. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to give a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be implemented by institutions in accordance with statutory regulations. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the Regional Government, society, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and/or in the form of discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. Any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually and psychologically, including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of statutory regulations. 18.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 24

In efforts to protect women victims of violence, the Regional Government is obligated to:
a. guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for women's protection and victim handling guarantees to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in women's protection efforts carried out by Regional Apparatus handling governmental affairs in the field of Women's Protection and Empowerment.

NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 27

2. Membership of the task force, forum, working group or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of related Regional Apparatus, community leaders, religious leaders, and universities.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Services is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim residents, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a technical operational implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or give access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for the needs of beneficiaries. 34. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by respect for human rights is respect, upholding the inherent human rights of citizens, and protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Point b What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing tribe, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or action for vulnerable women's groups with the aim of achieving equality of rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Point c What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to women and men. What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes equal, harmonious and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development and enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Point d What is meant by benefit is the implementation of women's protection that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Part Three

Services for Victims of Violence, Exploitation and Discrimination

Article 13

1. The implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of health as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (2) letter a is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of health.

25 -

(2) The form of empowerment in the field of health as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of reproductive and sexual health services that are healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.

3. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. health services during the pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum periods;
b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services and sexual health;
c. reproductive health services; and
d. services and provision of adequate lactation rooms at every regional government institution, public facilities and industries.
4. Health services as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out through promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative approaches.

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Services is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim residents, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a technical operational implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or give access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for the needs of beneficiaries. 34. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

REGIONAL SECRETARIAT OF SURAKARTA CITY YENI APRILIAWATI

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SURAKARTA CITY

NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of statutory regulations. 18.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Services is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim residents, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to give a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be implemented by institutions in accordance with statutory regulations. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the Regional Government, society, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and/or in the form of discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. Any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually and psychologically, including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

NUMBER 7 OF 2024

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of statutory regulations. 18.

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of statutory regulations. 18.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25. Integrated Services is the provision of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim residents, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a technical operational implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, exploitation, discrimination, and other problems. 33. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or give access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for the needs of beneficiaries. 34. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually and psychologically, including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Temporary Shelter is a service function to provide or give access to temporary protection places that prioritize security and safety, as well as clothing, food, and supporting facilities for the needs of beneficiaries. 34. Standard Operating Procedures hereinafter abbreviated as SOP are standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.

Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and role/condition as ordained, without discrimination. The fate of women victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women is often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, and environments located in industrial sectors.

Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, the regional government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT), which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment (P2TP), Safe House, Social Protection House (RPS), Trauma Center Protection House (RPTC), Women's Social Protection House (RPSW), Shelter House, etc., which specifically have the main duties and functions for the empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to implement efforts to protect women victims of violence through: implementing protection policies for women victims of violence applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women victims of violence, establishing PPT, ensuring the implementation of ease of service to victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in victim recovery efforts.

Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in government affairs that are the authority of the region; 5. Woman is a person of female gender starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 6. Protection is all efforts to fulfill rights and provide assistance to give a sense of security to witnesses and/or victims that must be implemented by institutions in accordance with statutory regulations. 7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the Regional Government, society, and/or other parties aimed at protecting women from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination as well as providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights. 8. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, cultural resources so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept and be free from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 9. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, educational, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 10. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 12. Violence Against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and/or in the form of discrimination, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. Any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually and psychologically, including certain acts of arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 13. Gender-Based Online Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBGO is violence that occurs through digital media or online platforms that targets women, including: comments or messages that are insulting, demeaning, or belittling Women; messages or comments that threaten to commit physical or sexual violence against Women; disseminating victims' personal information (such as addresses, telephone numbers, or other identities) without permission with the aim of intimidating or harming victims; extortion involving threats to spread intimate images or videos of victims unless victims meet the perpetrator's demands; spreading private photos or videos of an intimate nature without the consent of the women in the content; use of technology to stalk or monitor victims continuously, often with the aim of frightening or controlling victims; and digitally altering images or videos of women for the purpose of insulting, humiliating, or sexually exploiting. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim; restricting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs; prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence; using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment; and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of statutory regulations. 18.

Part Three

Purpose, Objectives and Scope

Article 31

1. To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the Region.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically from the planning stage up to the policies, programs and activities for the protection of women for the current year.
4. The results of monitoring as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be reported to the Mayor periodically.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 24

In efforts to protect women victims of violence, the Regional Government is obligated to:
a. guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for women's protection and victim handling guarantees to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in women's protection efforts carried out by Regional Apparatus handling governmental affairs in the field of Women's Protection and Empowerment.

Article 25

The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. implementing policies, programs, activities for women's protection to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for women's protection; and - 31 -
c. applying service standards for women's protection and SOPs.

Article 32

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection on a regular basis.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.

Article 14

1. Women's Empowerment in the field of education as referred to in Article 12 paragraph (2) letter b is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.
2. Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve women's capabilities.
3. Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (2) includes the provision of skills and job training.
